document.description: LptA is a soluble periplasmic lipopolysaccharide-binding and transfer protein that forms the central bridge of the Lpt trans-envelope machinery. It receives lipopolysaccharide from inner-membrane LptC and transfers it toward the LptDE outer-membrane translocon for outer-membrane assembly.

review.summary: LptA directly binds lipopolysaccharide while carrying it across the periplasm.
review.reason: The LptA family assignment and UniProt functional description support direct LPS binding. Experimental support is from the E. coli orthologue lptA (same PANTHER subfamily).

review.summary: LptE directly binds LPS within the LptDE outer-membrane translocon.
review.reason: LPS binding is supported by the LptE family assignment and UniProt functional description. Experimental support is from the E. coli orthologue lptE (same PANTHER subfamily).

supported_by.supporting_text: Binds LPS and may serve as the LPS recognition site at the outer membrane.
Our results establish that LptE binds LPS specifically and that this is crucial to LptE’s function in vivo.

review.summary: Lipidated LptE is localized to the cell outer membrane.
